timeline: Ch1: Summit begins at converted academy on cliff. 12 students from 12 countries gather in oak-paneled room with shuttered windows. Coordinator distributes earpieces for mandatory translation for seven days. Sofia Bellini assigned as translator for Elias van Doren, who has difficulty speaking. Yuki Tanaka observes Sofia's discomfort. No personal devices allowed; building runs on closed system. Beneath the floor, a constant mechanical hum.

Ch2: After Amara Okafor is found dead, Dmitri Ivanov theorizes the translation system kills those whose words are most mistranslated. Sofia Bellini volunteers as designated speaker and translator for the group. The remaining 11 students agree, establishing strict silence rules: no unnecessary conversation, no slang, no idioms.

Ch3: Two days after Amara's death, Dmitri Ivanov proposes and executes a nonsense experiment during the sunset silence window to test whether the system punishes all sound or only meaningful language. He speaks syllables.

Ch4: The group plays a recording of Lea saying a simple test sentence in English; translation is perfect. Lea is then found dead in her room with blood from her ear and earpiece still in. The theory that the system only kills mistranslated words is disproven. Sofia discovers a paper of rules that she never wrote, deepening the mystery.

Ch5: Pierre Leclerc reveals he is a journalist; shows a keycard found in the coordinator's office which later appeared on his pillow. The keycard opens the basement door, leading the group to decide Sofia and Yuki will explore the sub-basement archives. As the sunset silence window nears, they descend into a chamber lined with floor-to-ceiling shelves.

Ch6: Sofia and Yuki explore the archives and discover a hidden panel behind a shelf containing a cassette tape labeled 'Petrescu – original testimony' with still-wet ink. Using foam headphones, Sofia listens to a recording of an official interrogating a past participant, Nadia Petrescu, using 'clarification' to alter her testimony. They also find a transcript detailing hundreds of word alterations across sessions. Sofia realizes she has been doing the same thing to Elias by rephrasing his words, implicating herself in the system's mechanism.

Ch7: During nightly lockdown, Sofia and Elias are herded by shifting architecture and become trapped together in the interpreter booth. Sofia discovers a sticker on the microphone: 'Property of Department of Linguistic Correction, 1997.' She tells Elias about the Nadia Petrescu erasures. Elias, wanting to comfort her, speaks aloud a stammered sentence, which triggers Sofia’s automatic impulse to rephrase him. She barely stops herself.

Ch8: After the early replay ends, the interpreter booth unlocks and releases Sofia and Elias into a corridor lit by pulsing red emergency strips. The group gathers in the control-room desk. Sofia connects Elias's earpiece to a correction terminal, revealing two columns: Nadia Petrescu's recorded intervention events (47) and Elias van Doren's correction count (63). Yuki learns that Petrescu's 342 word alterations spanned 47 sessions; Pierre clarifies each correction event marks a single official intervention. Despite Lea's perfect translation accuracy, her entry shows 29 corrections, implying that interruptions or rephrasing may be the true metric for the system's deadly punishment. Sofia recognizes that her own corrections of Elias have been catalogued as violations.
